notes: model_revision: which measurement model produced a report. 1 — no dividend calendar; 2 — trades spanning an ex-dividend bar are marked (T2-22, ADR-025); 3 — entry filter removed and candle preparation shared by the backtest and live (T3-8b, ADR-028): the trade set grew from 929 to 1711, so reports before and after are not comparable. Re-running an old hypothesis on a corrected model is not a new trial, so n_trials stays, but the revision records that the numbers moved.
Thresholds for validation reports (heatmap, verdict). Every report prints them together with the fingerprint, so a decision can be reproduced.
min_trades_per_cell: cells with fewer closed trades do not take part in the plateau decision and are marked in the table.
plateau_margin_percent: a neighbour passes when its net expectancy is within this share of the best cell.
plateau_share: share of the 8 neighbours (±1 step on each axis) that must pass for the best cell to be called a plateau.
min_neighbours_evaluated: a corner cell has only 3 neighbours, so 3 is the floor that keeps every grid shape decidable; raise it for wider grids.
A plateau is reported only when the best cell and the passing neighbours are positive: a margin around a negative best cell means nothing.
min_total_trades: below this the multi-instrument run reports insufficient_trades instead of a verdict; 200 is the level where a per-trade confidence interval stops being anecdotal.
min_ticker_trades: a ticker below this is marked thin, stays in the totals and is excluded from the share of profitable tickers; 30 matches the heatmap cell floor.
block_days: calendar length of one bootstrap block; a block holds the trades of every ticker, so the common market factor is resampled together.
Empty blocks are part of the population: dropping them would bias the sample towards active periods.

gap_threshold_percent: a trade is marked gap_affected when an overnight gap inside its holding period exceeds this size. Candles are not dividend-adjusted, so an ex-dividend gap looks like a market move; the report prints totals with and without such trades instead of guessing ex-dividend dates.

verdict.min_total_trades / min_oos_trades: below either, the verdict is inconclusive. The OOS floor is 100, not 200: gates B4 and C4 still require the interval to be above zero, so a small sample is filtered by interval width rather than by a count.

verdict.holdout_start / holdout_end: frozen before the run and used as the out-of-sample period. A fixed-parameter walk-forward is not out-of-sample by parameters when the point was chosen on that same history, so the holdout is a separate calendar window.

verdict.cost_multiplier: the pool is re-run with every cost multiplied by this factor. A positive interval that turns fully negative at 2x costs is fragile, not rejected: the strategy is cost-sensitive, it was not measured negative at base costs.
verdict.tp_penalty_bps: TP is a limit order and pays no costs in the base model; this adds the penalty as a gate. If the interval at this penalty contains zero, the result is fragile.
verdict.oos_ratio_min_percent: OOS net bps below this share of the full-pool net bps means the result does not survive on data outside the fit window.
verdict.n_trials: declared number of parameter and structure variants tried before this report. Informational for now; it is the input a multiple-testing correction will need.

dividends.gap_match_ratio: an event is applied only when the ex-bar falls by at least this share of the expected dividend gap (dividend_gross / previous close). 0.3 means 'clearly less than half of the expected drop' - chosen as a sanity floor, not tuned to the sample. A price rise never counts as a match. Events below it are reported as no_gap_match and do not mark trades.

min_sample_trades: one floor for every decision that needs a minimum sample: a heatmap cell, a weekend trade group. Kept at the top level so the two checks cannot drift apart; a section may still override it locally (heatmap.min_trades_per_cell, used by the tests and the --min-trades flag).

weekend.start: MOEX weekend trading began in March 2025. Earlier bars are almost all weekday sessions, so a combined 'with and without weekend bars' total would mix two market regimes. The audit window starts here for every ticker; a ticker whose first weekend bar is later starts at that bar, because the set was expanded at different dates.

weekend.max_zero_volume_share: a weekend bar with volume == 0 had no trades. Above this share of the ticker's weekend bars in the window the weekend session is structurally unusable and the bars are excluded by a rule, not by the resulting net. 0.10 is a floor for 'the session trades', fixed before the run (ADR-031). The weekday-versus-weekend ratio is printed for information and is not decisive.

evaluate.target_edge_bps: the smallest per-trade effect worth trading after costs. 25 bps is set from the return target, not from what the current sample can measure: at sigma ~286 bps and ~280 trades a year, a per-trade edge of 25 bps gives an annual Sharpe near 1.5 before the correlation haircut and the live degradation, so 20 bps sits on the border and 25 keeps a margin (ADR-032). `rejected` means the interval proves the effect is BELOW this target, not that zero is not excluded.

evaluate.target_model: the target of an event idea comes from its own trade count, not from a single number for every strategy (ADR-034). target = sharpe_target * sigma / sqrt(trades a year) / live_retention, floored at cost_floor_bps. sigma is the unconditional dispersion of the outcome variable and the trade count is the number of eligible events, both measured before the strategy exists, so the target can be fixed before the run and stored next to the hypothesis. live_retention is the share of the backtest edge expected to survive execution; a target that exactly reaches the Sharpe goal leaves no room for that loss. cost_floor_bps is a round-trip cost: no idea below it is worth trading whatever the sample size.

evaluate.power: power of the minimum detectable effect. 0.80 is the standard: MDE = (z(1-alpha/2) + z(power)) * SE. The design table in docs/EVALUATE_DESIGN.md §5.1 was computed with 50% power (z only), so its numbers are ~1.43 times smaller; ADR-032 records both.
evaluate.screening_alpha: soft screening criterion on the fit window (CI 1-alpha). It filters dead ideas and never proves anything, so it does not need the strict level.
evaluate.confirm_alpha: confirmation level on the sealed period; the per-hypothesis level is confirm_alpha / k, where k is the number of sealed accesses recorded in the journal.

evaluate.sealed_start: first day of the sealed out-of-sample period. The evaluate loader never reads candles at or after this date unless the sealed period is opened explicitly; the row is not recorded and the period is printed as 'not accessed'.
evaluate.budget: ideas per calendar quarter, read from the journal. A budget in ideas, not in grid cells (ADR-029).
